newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI pulls down rupee against forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: India RBI pulls down rupee against forward dollar.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened heavily in the forward dollar market on Monday, pushing up forward premiums, even as the commerce minister said the rupee's appreciation against the U.S. currency was affecting Indian export competitiveness.
RBI's purchases pushed up premiums by almost 10 paise for January dollars, dealers said.
January dollars were quoted at 77/80 paise on Monday evening compared to the opening level of 69/70, they said.
The central bank bought forward dollars across wide maturities -- January, April and June, dealers said.
RBI also repeatedly hit the spot market.
Large dollar sales by a handful of foreign banks -- estimated at $150 million -- made RBI's spot intervention ineffective, dealers said.
These banks were selling the proceeds of a $150 million FRN raised by Indian Railway Finance Corp, the funding arm of Indian Railways, dealers said.
Spot dollar was at 35.732/740 rupees in latest quotes compared with 35.77/79, they said.
